newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Iran to boost Russian imports under wide agreement.
newsitem.headline: Iran to boost Russian imports under wide agreement.

text.p: Iran on Thursday signed a broad agreement to expand economic relations with Russia, including the purchase of tens of millions of dollars worth of Russian subway cars and technical equipment.
Officials from the two sides said future cooperation in the oil and gas industry would be important but did not give details of any specific projects.
The agreement was forged during the first meeting of the Russian-Iranian Commission for Economic Cooperation since the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991.

"Cooperation with Iran gives us, namely the Russian people, a big market for our industrial machine production, and gives us an opportunity to provide jobs," Deputy Prime Minister Oleg Davydov said at the signing.
"Iran is a market we are interested in developing for our industry," said Davydov, who is also Minister for Foreign Economic Relations.
Iran and Russia have recently expanded ties in several economic agreements.

Both countries on Thursday reaffirmed Russia's 1995 commitment to finishing the $800 million construction of Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant, a deal which has angered the United States and other nations.

"Naturally, there was an agreement on this (project) that remains in force," Iran's Economy and Finance Minister Morteza Mohammadkhan told reporters. "We see no limits on the two sides to limit cooperation in this area."
In a side agreement signed on Wednesday, Iran will purchase $15 million worth of subway cars for the Tehran underground from Moscow's Metromash factory, Davydov told Reuters.
Mohammadkhan said the agreement could be worth up to $50 or $60 million when including escalators and other equipment.

After talks between officials from several ministries and banks, Iran also signed a letter of intent for Russia to update technology in a steel plant in Isfahan, Russia's deputy minister of industry, Serafim Afonin, said.
The deal would be worth tens of millions of dollars, he said.
An important area of future cooperation is in oil and gas industries, Mohammadkhan said after signing the agreement, although officials did not provide details of concrete ventures.
Among possible future projects are joint exploration for oil in the Caspian Sea. Both ministers said, however, further talks on financing larger projects were needed.
In other signs of warming economic ties, Russia and Iran agreed to bar double taxation, and plan to open Iranian business and trade promotion offices in Moscow and several other cities.
Trade between the two countries more than doubled from 1994 to 1995, and was worth $200 million last year. Davydov said he expected the value of trade to nearly double in 1996.

"Just as we are interested in relations with Western countries even though we have some differences with them, we are also interested in relations with other countries like Iran with whom we have differences," a Russian transport official said.
Russia has also signaled a greater willingness to work with Iran on non-economic matters.

On Wednesday, Russia's Minister for Civil Defence and Emergencies Sergei Shoigu flew to Tehran to discuss cooperation in areas such as organising rescue operations during earthquakes, his spokeswoman said.
